About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you'll do

  • Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
  • Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
  • Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
  • Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
  • Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
  • Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

  • You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
  • You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
  • You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
  • You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
  • You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
  • You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.

We'd be thrilled if you had

  • Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.
  • Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.
  • Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You'll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.

Tensordyne Values

  • Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.
  • Own it and get it done. Take responsibility and drive results.
  • Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
  • Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.
  • Value different perspectives. The strongest teams challenge assumptions and bring diverse experience to difficult problems.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

A note to recruitment agencies: Please do not contact Tensordyne employees or leaders regarding this role. We do not accept unsolicited agency resumes and are not responsible for fees associated with unsolicited submissions.

Was wir dir bieten

Du hast die Chance, Teil eines hochinnovativen, agilen und einzigartigen Teams zu sein, das mit den renommiertesten Kunden im Automobilsektor zusammenarbeitet. Our Offer & Benefits

HEY THERE!

Ready to put our brand in front of millions of people worldwide? We’re looking for a Data Analyst, Marketing to turn raw campaign and engagement data into decisions — telling us which channels, markets, and customers to target next.

This isn’t a dashboard-building role. You’ll build robust data products, of course — but the real impact comes from the reporting and insight you deliver, and the incremental value that creates for the marketing team.

Let’s shape the future of nutrition together and make Yazio the most successful nutrition app worldwide!

This role is 100% remote and open to candidates based in Germany, Spain, Portugal, or the U.K.

YOUR MISSION

  • Show our Performance Marketing team which campaigns to double down on — and which to scale back.

  • Partner with our CRM team to learn what messaging resonates with each user segment, then run experiments to measure the uplift.

  • Own the data transformation process, from raw channel and MMP data to curated, ready-to-use datasets in our self-service BI tool.

  • Define requirements with Data Engineering to ingest new data sources.

  • Work with the Analytics team to build a data-driven culture across Yazio.

YOUR PROFILE

  • Hands-on experience with performance marketing data for a native mobile app, covering channel-level or MMP data (ideally both).

  • Solid grasp of attribution, incrementality, funnel and cohort analysis, plus marketing performance metrics like iROAS and CAC.

  • High proficiency in SQL and working knowledge of Python.

  • Solid experience in either analytics engineering (e.g., using dbt to transform data) or data science (e.g., geo-lift tests, holdout tests, A/B tests, media mix modeling). You don’t need both, but you should be strong in one.

OUR CORE TECH STACK

We use:

  • Snowflake as our core Analytics data warehouse.

  • dbt & Dagster to transform & orchestrate our data.

  • Growthbook to power experimentation.

  • Omni to provide self-service analytics.

  • Prefect to handle our ML workflows.

WHY US?

  • An exciting product with millions of users in over 150 countries, driven by our mission to transform the world through healthy eating

These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.

Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Every promise our products make to a user or merchant is kept by an internal team somewhere in the company. When those teams can organise their work, adapt quickly and stay focused, Wave moves fast; when they can't, the company slows down and customers feel it. When we were smaller, organizing work didn't take much more than a quick spreadsheet but that breaks at scale.

Wave is now the largest financial institution in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and the Gambia. We work with millions of users every month, employ thousands of people, and are growing rapidly. Similar processes now run in a dozen countries, but each team has built its own version, either because they don't know a better one exists or because setting it up well is harder than it should be.

AI has made this both better and worse: anyone can now build a workflow in an hour, but many aren't secure, won't scale, cost too much, or automate a process that should have been simplified first. Your job is to think from first principles about how work at Wave should run, give people a consistent and safe way to improve their own workflows, and make the common ones easy to adopt.

We're looking for a product manager who gets a kick out of figuring out how work should actually flow, and who doesn't much care whether the answer is a tool we build, a workflow in something we already pay for, or no tool at all. Someone who enjoys getting into the weeds with operations teams and who turns what they learn there into playbooks and building blocks every team can use.

In this role, you'll...

    • Own how Wave's general work tools get used. You're accountable for tools like Slack, Monday, and AI serving teams well. You work with the People team and other stakeholders to make sure they're set up so that organizing work or finding an answer is easy from day one. You help us make the right calls on major vendor decisions using what you've seen first-hand from users.
    • Help operations teams use AI efficiently and safely. You find the use cases where it truly saves teams time and turn those into shared skills, bots, and templates others can pick up in minutes. You build with these tools every day and teach teams to build in a secure and affordable way.
    • Care about the person, but solve for the company. There are far more problems than you can take on, so you pick the ones that help the most teams. You turn each solution into a playbook, template, or building block, and work through champions in every team to carry it forward.
    • Make sure each problem gets solved the right way. You're the expert on how people organize work in general, but behind every workflow sits domain context, constraints, and sometimes a product tool that already fits. You work with the leaders and PMs in that domain to decide whether a process should be simplified, automated, or shouldn't exist at all.
    • Build the team this work needs, starting with you. In your first few months you'll spend much of your time in-country with our operations teams as an IC, setting up workflows yourself with Slack and Monday.com, creating Claude skills and writing the first playbooks. As you learn more about what the company needs you can help us form a team around you.

Key Details

  • This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, USA, Canada, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso
  • Wave is a distributed team, and we fund up to three in-person get-togethers a year, in line with Wave's travel policy.
  • Remote team members are expected to travel to our operational markets (e.g. Senegal or Côte d'Ivoire) at least once per quarter. Exceptions apply, but we've found this key to understanding our users and product.
  • Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary between $142,200 - $203,300 USD, plus a generous equity package.
  • Major benefits:
    • Subsidised health insurance for you and your dependents, and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country).
    • 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidised fertility assistance.
    • Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days per year. 
    • $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

Requirement

  • 5+ years of experience in product management, or in a similar role where you owned products or processes end-to-end, ideally in high-ownership, fast-paced environments like scale-ups.
  • Proven success in overseeing all elements of the product development lifecycle, such as user research, design, implementation and evaluation
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience designing and improving operational workflows that save teams time, produce accurate results, and run reliably at a reasonable cost.
  • AI-fluent: you've used tools like Claude or ChatGPT to build skills, automations, or workflows that did something meaningful in your actual job, not just experiments.
  • Speak fluent English
  • Bonus if you
    • Speak at least conversational French
    • Have worked with Slack and an enterprise workflow tool like Monday, Jira or Linear.
    • Have worked in or closely with large operations teams (support, field, finance)
    • Are a mobile money user in Sub-Saharan Africa

You might be a good fit if you

  • Resonate deeply with how we do product and have experience working that way.
  • Are a strong communicator that can inspire and lead by influence.
  • Are great at coordinating across teams and excel at communicating across multiple cultures.
  • Have a good nose for user-focused product design and obsess over user experience.
  • Take ownership for outcomes and do whatever you can to make them close to inevitable.
  • Have strong instincts for asking questions that could move the needle.
  • Have the courage and persistence to replan when feedback or new information arrives.
  • Always listen with empathy but ruthlessly prioritize based on impact.
  • Are excited about travel and meet users where they are — your users will be in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and other countries in Africa, and some travel will be essential.

About Product at Wave

Product has always been very important to us at Wave, starting from day one with two very strong product-minded founders. Product Managers play a central role in our organization, impacting large chunks of the company around them, similar to the founders they were shaped after years ago.

Our approach to building products may not be what you've seen in other places. Our processes are lightweight, informed by principles instead of methodologies and our PMs don't just manage backlogs full of polished tickets. Read our write-up on product at Wave!

If you're excited to own a real problem end-to-end, set your own goals, and guide a team toward outcomes that matter for real people, you'll feel right at home here.

If that's you, we'd love to meet you.

 

Our team

  • We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.

  • We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue.

Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

As Omnea's Account Manager, you own the relationship with our customers across their entire lifecycle, working with some of our largest and most strategic accounts. Your job is to make sure customers get real, measurable value from Omnea from day one, and to turn that value into renewals, expansion, and upsell.

Omnea's product is sticky: it's a business transformation, not a point tool, so once a customer is live, expansion tends to follow. Your focus skews heavily toward that expansion motion, not just keeping accounts renewed.

You'll build deep, long-term relationships with your champions and become a trusted advisor to stakeholders at every level, from procurement managers up to CFOs. You'll be the internal voice of the customer, working closely with both technical and commercial teams to keep Omnea customer-centric at its core.

This is an early hire on the customer team, working directly with Abs, Ben, and Rebe to build the function from the ground up. There's no fixed playbook yet: you'll help write it.

What You'll Do

  • Own a revenue number: You'll carry an NRR quota covering both expansion and retention across your enterprise book. That means proactively identifying upsell opportunities, running commercial conversations at exec level, and owning the renewal process end-to-end.

  • Build relationships that go all the way to the top: Your relationships will run from procurement managers to CFOs. You'll multi-thread across each account, building genuine trust across multiple stakeholders, and you'll be the person customers call when something goes wrong or when they're thinking about what's next.

  • Build the playbook from scratch: There's no fully built playbook yet - you'll help shape it. You'll work alongside an exceptional implementation team, product experts, and leadership that have scaled world-class companies to define the commercial rhythms, norms, and processes to set the standard as the function grows.

  • Shape what Omnea builds next: You're the closest person to what our customers will and won't pay for. You'll feed that signal directly to Product and Revenue leadership, surfacing what's blocking adoption, what's driving expansion, and where we should be investing.

What's Different About This Role

  • This isn't a traditional post-sale account management role. Omnea's product is a business transformation, not a point tool, so most of your quota comes from expansion, not just renewal.

  • We're not looking for a narrow "Account Manager" background. We want people from GTM roles broadly or from customer-facing roles with heavy commercial/GTM crossover.

  • There's no fully built playbook. You'll define the commercial rhythms and processes as you go, working directly with Abs, Ben, and Rebe.

  • You'll be as close to the product roadmap as anyone outside Product itself: what you hear from customers directly shapes what gets built next.

About You

We don't expect you to know exactly how to do all of this when you join. We're looking for someone with the right attitude and skillset to take this on.

TL;DR: you're commercially sharp, and you instinctively know how to navigate complex organisations. You might come from a GTM role (sales, customer success, partnerships) or a customer-facing role with heavy GTM crossover. What matters is that you've worked in real enterprise environments, managed senior stakeholders with high expectations, and have a track record of getting things done.

  • 4-8 years of experience in a top-tier, fast-paced environment: a startup, scale-up, VC, consulting, banking, or something you built yourself

    • If you've been in a commercial role, you've worked six-figure ARR+ accounts, navigated multi-stakeholder buying committees, and built genuine executive relationships

  • You build rapport, influence people, and drive change, whether with a distinguished exec or a junior operator. You have the gravitas to engage senior leadership, ideally up to CFOs, Legal, or Procurement

  • You're comfortable in ambiguity. You don't need a fully built playbook: you'll build it as you go and improve it as you learn. You're organised enough to manage a complex book of business without dropping anything, and confident enough to push back on customers when they're wrong

  • You're ambitious, competitive, and care about doing excellent work, with a track record of high performance in whatever you've turned your hand to: sales, academia, sport, or something of your own. You take ownership seriously, and you'd rather work hard on something meaningful than coast on something safe

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to define and drive the technical direction of XTM One, Filigran's AI platform for threat informed defense and the agentic core of the XTM Suite.

XTM One creates and runs cybersecurity expert AI agents and dispatches their intelligence across OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenGRC. It also hosts the suite's shared commons (unified authentication, consolidated datasets, configuration) and ships both as SaaS and on premises. Every XTM product connects to it, which makes its architecture one of the most structuring technical decisions at Filigran.

This is not a management role: no headcount, no sprints. You own the technical craft, standards and vision of XTM One, and you carry them into the XTM Foundation, where the engineering principles shared by all products are set for the 60+ engineers at Filigran.

💼 Your Responsibilities

Vision & architecture

  • Arbitrate key decisions on scalability, resilience, security, maintainability and cost, including LLM latency and inference cost.

Standards & quality

  • Define the team's technical principles (architecture patterns, code quality, tooling, CI/CD, testing, development with AI assistants) and get them applied through docs, reviews, pairing and example.

  • Keep the right balance between features, technical debt and innovation.

Integration across products & XTM Foundation

  • Define how OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenGRC and future products integrate with XTM One: contracts, authentication, data exchange, versioning.

  • Be a full member of the XTM Foundation: bring the XTM One perspective in, carry its decisions back, and keep coherence with the other Principal and Staff Engineers.

In the code

  • Write production code, prototype new approaches before the team adopts them, review critical PRs so that feedback teaches, and unblock engineers.

  • Reports to: VP of Technology

  • Key collaborators: XTM One engineering team and its verticals; XTM Foundation (Principal and Staff Engineers across OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenGRC); Product leadership; open source contributors.

  • Working model: embedded in the XTM One team, with regular XTM Foundation work.

  • Bonus: cybersecurity domain knowledge (CTI, CTEM, MITRE ATT&CK, STIX/TAXII); extensible plugin or tool ecosystems; open source contributions or maintainership.

    About the role

    As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week.

    You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver.

    At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive.

    What You'll Do

    • Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
    • Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people.
    • Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do.
    • Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source.
    • Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business.
    • Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence.
    • Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge.
    • Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question.
    • Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake.
    • Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us.

    Requirements

    What You’ll Need

    Requirements

    • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
    • 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's.
    • Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously.
    • Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does.
    • Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams.
    • Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope.
    • Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there.
    • Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases.
    • Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI.
    • Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus.
    • Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it.
    • Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up.
    • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

    Who You Are

    You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head.

    You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide.     We are looking for an experienced Senior Integration Software Engineer to bring our algorithms and software backend together into reliable, operational solutions, and to take technical ownership of how our software is integrated.

    Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence.

    We are expanding our R&D team with an Integration Software Engineer who enjoys building clean, reliable interfaces between components and working where software meets hardware, and who takes ownership of making complex systems work together end to end.

    As a Senior Integration Software Engineer, you will support their integration into operational systems: connecting algorithms to the backend through robust APIs, building data connectors, health reporting and control software, and defining and verifying integrations with Command and Control (C2) systems.

    You will work closely with domain experts in acoustics, signal processing and machine learning, and with the software engineering team, and hands-on with our monitoring systems at our headquarters and production facility. You will also take technical ownership of work delivered by internal and external engineers and set the standard for good engineering practices.

    Key Responsibilities

    • Lead software integration engineering for our underwater acoustic sensing systems, ensuring frontend and backend components, algorithms, and hardware systems work together reliably.

    • Integrate the algorithmic toolbox with our system backends, turning research code into maintainable, versioned and deployable software components.

    • Implement data interfaces for our real-time sonar processing pipeline, to ingest multiple sensors (acoustic, heading, temperature, pressure, etc.) from internal and external data acquisition systems. Implement health reporting, logging and monitoring, so that the status and performance of software and system components is visible and actionable.

    • Develop the software control layer for our sensing systems and their hardware components, including APIs for commanding, state handling, error handling and recovery.

    • Implement, align and verify software integrations with external partners and C2 systems, being directly involved in defining interfaces, maintaining interface specifications and running joint integration tests.

    • Testing & debugging: Develop system-level test suites and CI/CD pipelines, diagnose communication failures, and ensure secure, reliable data transfers as the toolbox and backends evolve.

    • Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers.

    • Work hands-on with integrated software and hardware systems at our headquarters and production facility, with occasional on-site visits.

    • Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team.

    Why Join Us?

    • Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups.

    • Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization.

    • Competitive salary and benefits package.

    • Enjoy regular team activities and company events.

    • Fresh team lunches provided 5 times/week.


    Qualifications:

    • BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.

    • Significant professional experience in software engineering, with a focus on system integration, backend or platform development.

    • Extensive experience developing production software in Python, including packaging, testing, dependency management and writing maintainable, well-structured code.

    • Familiarity with systems programming in C++, or Rust, for the purpose of extending Python for more performance or hardware control.

    • Proven experience designing and implementing APIs and messaging interfaces (e.g. MQTT, WebSocket) and data serialization (e.g. protobuf).

    • Experience with realtime data pipelines, and handling high-throughput or streaming data.

    • Experience with Docker, CI/CD and automated testing in a Linux environment.

    • Experience working with software that interacts with physical systems, and comfort doing hands-on integration and troubleshooting in a lab or production environment.

    • Experience reviewing code and designs, mentoring junior engineers, and setting engineering standards.

    • An outcome-focused mindset, with the ability to own a problem end to end or break it down for others.

    • Ability to work with algorithm developers and translate research code into robust, maintainable software.

    • Flexible and proactive in taking on what needs to be addressed, and comfortable in a fast-paced scale-up environment.

    • Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners.

    • Willingness to work primarily from our Amsterdam headquarters, as parts of the role involve classified information and physical systems.

    Nice to Have:

    • Knowledge of defense systems or defense standards (e.g. NATO STANAGs, MIL-STD), for example in naval, maritime security or surveillance systems.

    • Experience with the scientific Python stack (e.g. NumPy, SciPy) or integrating signal processing or ML models into production systems.

    • Experience developing software interfaces for controlling instruments or devices.

    • Experience with other messaging or streaming frameworks (e.g. Kafka, ZeroMQ, DDS).

    • Familiarity with observability tooling.

    Security & Compliance:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              About Griffin<\/strong><\/h2>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Hi, we\u2019re Griffin. We\u2019re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We\u2019ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We\u2019re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Learn more about what we do<\/a><\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Our culture<\/strong><\/h3>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don\u2019t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and<\/em> home life.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We understand that our culture and ways of working aren\u2019t for everyone, and we\u2019re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don\u2019t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Learn more about our culture.<\/a><\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The team<\/strong><\/h3>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Infrastructure sits within the Craft function. We\u2019re a small team of three - two engineers and an engineering manager - who work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner<\/a>. It\u2019s our job to build the foundations that everything else at Griffin runs on: the systems, the tooling, the automation that helps us run a highly resilient and reliable platform and lets other teams ship fast. We're a software engineering team as much as an infrastructure team: we write the code that runs our platform, not just the configuration around it.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              When we start work, we explore multiple solutions before picking one. We write RFCs, build proof-of-concepts, and run experiments to validate approaches. Once we commit to building something, we care about maintainability more than cleverness, observability more than hoping it works, and scalability over premature optimisation. We take the necessary time to ship quality solutions rather than hitting arbitrary deadlines. Once something goes live, we refactor the rough edges rather than polish what's already working.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The opportunity<\/strong><\/h3>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Day to day, you'll build and manage the infrastructure the bank runs on - both in the cloud and on our own hardware in third party data centres. This means running FoundationDB clusters and writing the software and tooling for hitless upgrades, managing Kubernetes, writing infrastructure as code in Pulumi and CDK, running the Bazel build farm, and owning the deployment pipeline from CI to production.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Operational resilience is a big part of the job: replica clusters, multi-region failover, and chaos engineering to test how systems handle failures. Security access, CircleCI pipelines, DataDog integration, and cloud spend all fall under infrastructure too.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              On our roadmap currently is: building out our self-hosted infrastructure to support a hybrid-cloud setup and remove single-vendor reliance, improving how Kubernetes scales, improving the build farm, and building out our PKI infrastructure. We also have plans for a global HTTP routing layer to allow seamless failover between sites. Much of this is software we built ourselves, and you'll shape it from the first design through to production.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Our infrastructure as code is written in TypeScript. Where it makes sense, tooling gets written in Clojure. There's some Rust too.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              What success looks like<\/strong><\/h3>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Infrastructure problems become production problems fast. Success here means thinking ahead - identifying issues with scale, security, or compliance before they affect services.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              You've eliminated an entire class of incidents by fixing the underlying architectural issue. You've proven the database and compute platform can handle 10x current traffic volumes by working with backend teams to stress-test it. You've cut deploy times in half by rethinking how the pipeline works. You've tested multi-region failover under realistic failure scenarios and it worked. <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              You've shipped well-tested software that turns risky manual operations, like database upgrades, into routine, hitless ones that the whole team maintains with confidence.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              You've redesigned service discovery to remove networking issues that used to cause weekly firefights. When new FCA requirements dropped, you were already compliant because you'd built the infrastructure to handle it months earlier.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              <\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              To do this, you'll own<\/strong><\/h3>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                <\/p><\/li><\/ul>

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

Chess.com is one of the largest gaming sites in the world and the #1 platform for playing, learning, and enjoying chess.

We are a team of 600+ fully remote people in 60+ countries working hard to serve the global chess community. We are here to support 250M+ chess players worldwide with the best possible product, content, and tools to serve the community!

We are a tech company. A gaming company. A content company. And we do it all with passion and commitment to the game. Above all we prize our mission-driven, flat, life-celebrating, no-corporate culture, and we look forward to meeting you and learning more about what you can bring to the team.

About The Role

The Cloud Engineer role is critical to scaling Chess.com's infrastructure to support millions of daily chess games and serve global users. This position combines site reliability engineering expertise with cloud infrastructure management, directly impacting system performance, reliability, and scalability across Chess.com's multi-regional distributed architecture. The role requires deep technical expertise in both infrastructure automation and application optimization to maintain Chess.com's position as a high-traffic gaming platform while enabling rapid feature development and deployment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Architect and optimize cloud-native infrastructure using Kubernetes, Terraform, and GitOps tools to support millions of concurrent chess games across multiple global regions
  • Lead performance optimization initiatives by analyzing Golang and TypeScript codebases to identify and resolve bottlenecks at scale, with specific focus on chess programming optimizations
  • Design and implement multi-regional resilient systems capable of handling extreme scale challenges including managing 1 million+ CPUs across dozens of regions
  • Run and evolve our private Kubernetes cloud on bare-metal: a Rancher-managed fleet in our own datacenters that carries compute and IO intensive workloads, operated as one platform with GKE regions, with workloads placed wherever they get the best cost and performance.
  • Execute incident response and operational excellence serving as primary technical resource for critical infrastructure issues, ensuring rapid resolution and minimal downtime
  • Develop high-performance integration patterns for distributed systems handling extensive data volumes while maintaining reliability and scalability targets
  • Collaborate with development teams to implement cloud service integration best practices and optimize application deployment architectures
  • Implement Infrastructure as Code practices using Terraform to manage all cloud resources, ensuring consistent, automated, and scalable deployment processes
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines with GitOps approaches using tools like ArgoCD to enable rapid, reliable software delivery
  • Monitor and enhance system observability through implementation of modern monitoring stacks including Prometheus, Mimir, ES, Vector and Tempo

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience managing large-scale, cloud-native distributed systems with proven ability to handle high-traffic production environments
  • Expert-level proficiency with Kubernetes including cluster deployment, management, and advanced orchestration patterns
  • Advanced Infrastructure as Code experience with Terraform for managing complex cloud and Kubernetes resources in production
  • Strong programming skills in Golang with demonstrated ability to optimize high-performance services and troubleshoot complex codebases
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems design including failure modes, architectural principles, and data modeling strategies
  • Extensive experience with major cloud platforms (GCP, AWS) including advanced services, networking, and cost optimization
  • Proficiency with GitOps and CI/CD methodologies using modern deployment automation and continuous integration practices
  • Hands-on experience with observability tools including metrics, logging, and distributed tracing systems for high-scale environments
  • Strong Linux systems administration skills with deep knowledge of system internals and performance optimization
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills for working effectively in globally distributed teams

Preferred Skills and Qualifications

  • Chess programming and optimization experience including bit-level manipulations and performance tuning for gaming applications
  • TypeScript development experience for full-stack infrastructure and tooling development
  • Service mesh implementation experience particularly in hybrid multi-cloud and bare-metal environments
  • Message broker expertise with systems like Kafka, PubSub, and Redis for event-driven architectures
  • Gaming industry experience with understanding of real-time systems and high-concurrency requirements
  • Experience with Google Cloud partnerships and direct collaboration with cloud provider engineering teams
  • C/C++ programming experience for low-level system optimizations
  • Advanced networking knowledge for multi-regional infrastructure and hybrid cloud connectivity
  • Experience managing bare-metal infrastructure and integrating with cloud-native services
  • Database performance optimization experience with large-scale data systems and indexing strategies

About the Opportunity

Here at Youth4Youth, we have grown a strong, tight-knit community of individuals who are passionate about making a difference and improving the lives of young people across the UK. Our growing team of volunteers all contribute, significantly, to the impact that we have as a charity on our direct beneficiaries, regardless of the department that they work in of the level of time that they are able to commit. Our servicesprimarily offer a peer-support network to young people right across the UK, allowing them to access a peer mentor who is of a similar age to them and somebody that they feel more comfortable speaking with.

If successful, you will be joining a growing team of diverse, but likeminded individuals, collaborating to increase the reach of the Charity and improve support provisions available to young people. All of our volunteers and employees are remote workers,but that doesn't stop us keeping in touch and maintaining a strong positive culture amongst our whole team.

About the role

Youth4Youth is seeking new Trustees for its Board as it continues to grow its impact at a national level. As a Trustee, you will have a unique and exciting opportunity to shape the future of the charity, whilst ensuring that we are governed effectively. We are Looking to appoint 4 - 5 new Trustees to our Board, and we are particularly interested in hearing from you if you have experience in the following areas:

  • Safeguarding, particularly in digital spaces

  • Fundraising

  • Commercial Development / Growth

As a youth focussed charity, we are committed to ensuring that Youth Voice is at the heart of every decision that we make. Alongside those experienced in the above areas, we are seeking individuals aged 25 and under to represent their peers on our Board, ensuring that Youth Voice is heard at every level.

If you would like to have an informal chat with the Chair of the Board prior to submitting an application, please reach out to .

Responsibilities and commitment

As a Trustee, we would ask that you are able to commit approximately 2 - 4 hours per month of your time. This may include:

  • Attending monthly Board connect meetings, hosted remotely (1 Hour)

  • Attending quarterly Board meetings (1.5 hours)

  • Attendance at any relevant committees, role specific

  • Attending an annual Development Day (1 full day)

Due to the make-up of our Board, all scheduled meetings fall outside of standard working hours, usually falling in evenings and weekends. This is subject to change based on the majority preferences of the Board.

As a Trustee, we would expect you to:

  • Challenge the status quo, leveraging your expertise to support the ongoing development and growth of a rapidly changing, but much needed charitable organisation.

  • Ensure that the Charity is governed correctly, in line with its governing document and charity law.

  • Support the development of future strategies which will enable further growth, and create sustainable, long-lasting impact.

  • Get involved as a volunteer, as required and in line with your availability, to support the CEO and other members of the organisation.

You will be joining a well established Board of Trustees who are all driven to create meaningful impact for young people across the UK. Our current Board of Trustees is chaired by the founder of Youth4Youth, Josh Towers, and is made up of an additional 5 Trustees. There is also an additional, newly formed, Commercial Trading Subsidiary Board (Y4Y Trading Ltd), chaired by a long-standing Trustee, Barney Harrison.

Supporting the organisation operationally is our CEO, Richard Nuttall and Operations Manager, Dora Botta. The remainder of a team is a mix of a very small paid team, but the organisation is primarily supported by volunteers.

Our mission is to continue to grow towards becoming one of the best charities in the UK. Our aim is to do this by building a diverse team, rich with different backgrounds and perspectives. About Us

We are a modern marketing collective built for scale, efficiency, and impact. As the parent company, Agital supports three specialized agencies: Go Fish Digital, REQ, and WDG, with shared infrastructure, advanced technology, and deeply experienced people, allowing each brand to do its best work.

Go Fish Digital is an engineering-forward performance marketing agency specializing in SEO, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), its Barracuda AI platform, social commerce, and conversion-focused creative.

WDG designs and builds complex enterprise web experiences for associations, nonprofits, foundations, universities, and other mission-driven organizations.

REQ is a digital marketing and communications agency specializing in brand, reputation, and advocacy for global organizations across technology, healthcare, finance, hospitality, and real estate.

Together, we operate as one collaborative ecosystem, combining deep expertise, AI-powered capabilities, and a culture of curiosity to help ambitious brands grow while creating meaningful opportunities for our people.

About the Role

Go Fish Digital is building a focused, integrated go-to-market engine to accelerate growth across our digital and performance marketing services. We’re looking for a detail-oriented Demand Generation Coordinator to support campaign execution and the marketing operations that drive qualified mid-market pipeline. This hands-on role combines campaign delivery, HubSpot administration, list management, content distribution, and foundational reporting.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Demand Generation, you’ll work closely with Product Marketing, Sales, and GTM Operations to turn campaign plans into accurate, timely execution. You’ll also collaborate with specialists across paid media, SEO/GEO, creative, and web development to help campaigns reach the right buyers and run reliably from launch through follow-up. This role suits someone eager to build practical skills in demand generation, marketing automation, and campaign analysis while helping build a more effective growth engine.

What You'll Do

Execute Campaigns and Email Programs

  • Build, test, schedule, and deploy marketing emails in HubSpot using approved messaging and campaign plans.
  • Configure campaign assets, forms, landing pages, and tracking links using established templates and processes.
  • Perform pre-launch checks on links, formatting, personalization, audience selection, suppression lists, and tracking.
  • Support coordinated marketing, BDR, and seller outreach through timely campaign setup and audience preparation.

Support Marketing Operations and Automation

  • Build and maintain campaign workflows, nurture sequences, and enrollment rules under the direction of the Senior Director of Demand Generation.
  • Maintain consistent campaign naming, asset organization, documentation, and tracking practices.
  • Monitor workflow execution and campaign handoffs, investigate routine issues, and escalate problems promptly.
  • Partner with GTM Operations on data quality, lead routing checks, and troubleshooting. Support established CRM processes and coordinate changes to integrations or system architecture with GTM Operations.

Manage Lists and Audience Segmentation

  • Prepare, clean, import, and segment contact and account lists based on campaign criteria.
  • Maintain contact properties, deduplication, subscription preferences, and suppression lists using established processes.
  • Check audience fit against agreed company, industry, geography, and buyer criteria before campaign launch.
  • Help monitor email bounces, unsubscribes, and other deliverability signals and flag issues for review.

Distribute Content and Coordinate Delivery

  • Publish and distribute approved content through email, website tools, social channels, and other campaign touchpoints.
  • Adapt approved assets to channel templates and coordinate with Content and agency specialists on required updates.
  • Maintain the campaign calendar, track deadlines and dependencies, and follow up on outstanding deliverables.
  • Support webinar and event execution, including registration pages, reminders, attendee lists, and follow-up campaigns.

Maintain Reporting and Improve Execution

  • Maintain basic campaign reports covering delivery, engagement, conversions, and downstream outcomes using established dashboards.
  • Check tracking and data completeness and surface gaps that affect reporting.
  • Support A/B tests by configuring approved variants, checking setup, and compiling results.
  • Identify ways to improve campaign accuracy, repeatability, and turnaround time.

What You Will Need

  • Relevant experience: 1–3 years of experience in marketing coordination, campaign execution, email marketing, or marketing operations, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Marketing platform skills: Hands-on experience building emails, managing lists, or supporting workflows in HubSpot or a comparable marketing automation platform.
  • Attention to detail: Able to catch errors in audience selection, data, links, copy, and campaign setup before launch.
  • Organization and follow-through: Able to manage multiple deadlines, maintain clear documentation, and communicate blockers early.
  • Data skills: Comfortable using spreadsheets to clean lists, organize information, and summarize basic campaign results.
  • Learning mindset: Curious about how campaigns and systems work, receptive to feedback, and eager to develop marketing operations skills.

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Experience with HubSpot workflows, forms, landing pages, campaign reporting, and Salesforce-connected processes.
  • Familiarity with B2B demand generation, lead lifecycle stages, email deliverability, and contact subscription management.
  • Experience building and implementing measurement, testing, and attribution methodologies
  • Experience supporting content distribution, webinars, or coordinated sales and marketing campaigns.

Why Join Us
You'll work alongside talented people who are passionate about solving problems, helping clients grow, and delivering meaningful results. We're a collaborative, fast-moving team where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed, and great work is recognized.

We believe the best work happens when people are trusted to take ownership, supported in their growth, and empowered to bring their unique perspectives to the table. Whether you're just getting started or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact while continuing to learn and grow.

Benefits & Compensation 

We believe great people deserve great support. Our company offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, well-being, and career growth, including:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Flexible work environment
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Unlimited paid time off
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • Paid parental leave
  • A collaborative culture with autonomy and ownership
