      <title>Upgrade: AI Experience Engineer (Conversational AI)</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Back-End Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Canada (Remote)
</p>

<p><span><strong>About the Role:</strong><br><br>An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.</span></p>
<p><span>We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. </span><span>You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.</span></p>
<p><span>Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span><strong>Our Core Technologies</strong></span></p>
<p><span>Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span><strong>What You'll Do</strong></span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Journey creation:</strong> Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Optimization:</strong> Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Edge case handling: </strong>Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Containment:</strong> Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Product partnership:</strong> Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Safety and compliance:</strong> Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Handoffs:</strong> Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Testing:</strong> Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Monitoring: </strong>Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Voice tuning:</strong> Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone</span></p>
<p><span>• <strong>Sierra relationship: </strong>Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span><strong>What We Look For:</strong></span></p>
<p><span>• 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles</span></p>
<p><span>• Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails</span></p>
<p><span>• Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates</span></p>
<p><span>• Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes</span></p>
<p><span>• Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.</span></p>
<p><span>• Product and customer mindset: you understand ops procedures, you read transcripts, care about tone, and measure success by whether the customer's problem got solved</span></p>
<p><span>• Ownership in production: rollouts, monitoring, log analysis and incident response</span></p>
<p><span>• Clear writing and the ability to work with non-engineers in operations, compliance and legal</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span><strong>Nice To Have:</strong></span></p>
<p><span>• Hands-on experience with Sierra Agent Studio, or a comparable no-code agent platform (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect)</span></p>
<p><span>• Voice AI experience: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, latency tuning, barge-in handling</span></p>
<p><span>• Contact center systems such as Genesys, and agent handoff design</span></p>
<p><span>• Background in fintech or another regulated industry (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2)</span></p>
<p><span>• Conversation design or UX writing experience</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span><strong>What We Offer You:&nbsp;</strong></span></p>
<p><span>• Competitive salary ($140K-$180K CAN) and stock option plan</span></p>
<p><span>• Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance&nbsp;</span></p>
<p><span>• Flexible PTO</span></p>
<p><span>• Opportunities for professional growth and development<br>• Paid parental leave</span></p>
<p><span>• Health &amp; wellness initiatives</span></p>

      <title>Cigna Healthcare: Clinical Program Senior Advisor - Remote - Express Scripts (Academic Detailing)</title>
      <region>USA Only</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Missouri, United States
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="http://www.cigna.com">http://www.cigna.com</a>
</p>

<h2><b>POSITION SUMMARY</b></h2><h2></h2><p>The Senior Clinical Consultant, Academic Detailing supports Evernorth’s Provider Engagement strategy by using clinical expertise, advanced analytics, and evidence-based prescriber education to identify and act on opportunities that improve medication use, quality, safety, and affordability. This role evaluates pharmacy and medical data, provider prescribing patterns, medication regimens, and client priorities to develop targeted, provider-facing academic detailing outreach that supports trend management, reduces waste, and advances measurable clinical and financial outcomes.</p><h2></h2><h2><b>LOCATION: REMOTE</b></h2><h2></h2><h2><b>ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS</b></h2><ul><li><p>Analyze pharmacy claims, medical data, provider prescribing patterns, utilization trends, and client-specific priorities to identify actionable clinical, quality, safety, and financial opportunities.</p></li><li><p>Develop, document, and execute evidence-based academic detailing strategies, including patient-specific clinical opportunity identification and provider-specific intervention plans aligned to clinical guidelines, formulary strategy, benefit design, and client objectives.</p></li><li><p>Deliver customized prescriber education through provider-facing channels such as telephonic consultation, clinical direct messaging, fax, written materials, grand rounds, or other approved outreach methods to support clinically appropriate, cost-effective medication use.</p></li><li><p>Use Evernorth analytic tools and reporting resources to improve targeting, monitor outreach activity, assess prescribing trends, and evaluate clinical and financial impact over time.</p></li><li><p>Provide provider-facing recommendations related to initiation, continuation, discontinuation, regimen simplification, dose optimization, formulary alternatives, adherence barriers, and other medication therapy opportunities within approved protocols and clinical guidance.</p></li><li><p>Partner with clients, account teams, clinical subject matter experts, and internal stakeholders to prioritize initiatives, align outreach topics, integrate client-specific processes, and support transparent reporting of progress and outcomes.</p></li><li><p>Maintain accurate documentation of outreach activity, provider feedback, intervention status, and projected or realized impact to support client reporting, operational continuity, and program improvement.</p></li><li><p>Contribute to staff meetings, quality workgroups, client discussions, and departmental initiatives by sharing insights, best practices, outcomes, barriers, and opportunities to improve provider engagement effectiveness.</p></li><li><p>Support formal and informal training, mentoring, and professional development activities, including development or delivery of education for peers, providers, clients, or internal partners.</p></li><li><p>Serve as a clinical resource for provider engagement initiatives and perform other related responsibilities as needed to support client priorities, departmental goals, and Evernorth’s broader clinical strategy.</p></li></ul><p></p><h2><b>QUALIFICATIONS</b></h2><ul><li><p>Current pharmacist license required; relevant PBM, managed care, health plan, provider engagement, or clinical program experience preferred.</p></li><li><p>Strong clinical knowledge and ability to interpret medication therapy, prescribing patterns, utilization trends, quality metrics, and evidence-based guidelines.</p></li><li><p>Experience using claims data, reporting tools, dashboards, or analytic platforms to identify opportunities, support decision-making, and measure outcomes.</p></li><li><p>Client management, consultative communication, or provider-facing education experience preferred.</p></li><li><p>Excellent verbal, presentation, and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex clinical and data insights into clear, actionable recommendations for providers, clients, and internal partners.</p></li><li><p>Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities, organize work independently, meet deadlines, and resolve complex issues.</p></li><li><p>Demonstrated collaboration, leadership, accountability, and commitment to service excellence, continuous improvement, and measurable outcomes.</p></li><li><p>Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn and effectively use internal reporting, documentation, and analytic tools.</p></li><li><p>Ability to work independently in a remote environment while actively collaborating with cross-functional teams and client stakeholders.</p></li></ul><p></p><br><p></p>If you will be working at home occasionally or permanently, the internet connection must be obtained through a cable broadband or fiber optic internet service provider with speeds of at least 10Mbps download/5Mbps upload.<p></p><p></p>For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary of 116,200 - 193,600 USD / yearly, depending on relevant factors, including experience and geographic location.<p></p><p></p><p>This role is also anticipated to be eligible to participate in an annual bonus plan.</p><br><p>At The Cigna Group, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive range of benefits, with a focus on supporting your whole health. Starting on day one of your employment, you’ll be offered several health-related benefits including medical, vision, dental, and well-being and behavioral health programs. We also offer 401(k), company paid life insurance, tuition reimbursement, a minimum of 18 days of paid time off per year, paid holidays, and leaves of absence. For more details on our employee benefits programs, <a href="https://jobs.thecignagroup.com/us/en/benefits"><span>click here</span></a>. </p><br><br><br><br><p><b>About The Cigna Group </b></p><p></p>Doing something meaningful starts with a simple decision, a commitment to changing lives. At The Cigna Group, we’re dedicated to improving the health and vitality of those we serve. Through our divisions Cigna Healthcare and Evernorth Health Services, we are committed to enhancing the lives of our clients, customers and patients. Join us in driving growth and improving lives.<p></p><p></p><p><i>Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, age, disability, sex, childbirth (including pregnancy) or related medical conditions including but not limited to lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, religion, national origin, ancestry, marital or familial status, genetic information, status with regard to public assistance, citizenship status or any other characteristic protected by applicable equal employment opportunity laws.</i></p><p></p><p></p><p><span><i>If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete the online application process, please email </i></span><a href="mailto:seeyourself@thecignagroup.com"><span><i><b>seeyourself@thecignagroup.com</b></i></span></a><span><i> for assistance.&nbsp; Please note that this email inbox is dedicated to accommodation requests only and cannot provide application updates or accept resumes.</i></span></p><p></p><p></p><p><i>The Cigna Group has a tobacco-free policy and reserves the right not to hire tobacco/nicotine users in states where that is legally permissible. Candidates in such states who use tobacco/nicotine will not be considered for employment unless they enter a qualifying smoking cessation program prior to the start of their employment. These states include: Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nebraska, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah, Vermont, and Washington State.</i></p><p></p><p></p><p><i><span>Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment in a manner </span><span>consistent with all federal, state and local ordinances.</span> </i></p>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/cigna-healthcare-clinical-program-senior-advisor-remote-express-scripts-academic-detailing">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/cigna-healthcare-clinical-program-senior-advisor-remote-express-scripts-academic-detailing</a></p>

      <title>Databricks: Deployment Strategist</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - India
</p>

<h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2>
<p>The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) team is a new, strategic initiative sponsored from the CEO and Founders down. Our mission is to win C-suite-sponsored, high-value AI opportunities by selling and delivering <em>outcomes</em>, not just a platform.</p>
<p>You will be part of the founding team, embedded with our most strategic customers from the very first sales call, all the way through to a production-ready solution. You will be the "product manager" for the customer's problem, responsible for the "why" and "what," while our FDEs (Engineers) will be your partners responsible for the "how."</p>
<h2><strong>Role Description</strong></h2>
<p>As a Deployment Strategist (DS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million-dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the technical and product direction of the engagement from initial discovery through production launch and adoption.</p>
<p>You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing. You will also lead technical discovery, shape solution architecture with FDEs, and ensure that each proposed solution can move from prototype to production.</p>
<p>This role requires a rare combination of executive presence, deep product thinking, technical depth, and a hands-on delivery mindset.</p>
<h2><strong>The impact you will have</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>C-Suite Scoping &amp; Value Definition:</strong> Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value of $10M+ problems, and define the pilot, including its MVP, success criteria, and timeline.</li>
<li><strong>End-to-End Product Ownership:</strong> Author the PRD, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope, and act as the primary hands-on QA tester. Translate business requirements into clear data, integration, security, and operational requirements that engineers can build against.</li>
<li><strong>Technical Solution Leadership</strong><strong> &amp; Delivery:</strong> Drive the FDE build team through an agile delivery process, manage stakeholders from the C-suite to individual engineers, and unblock technical or organizational issues. Lead technical discovery and design reviews. Understand the customer's data flows, integrations, platform constraints, and operational environment; pressure-test architecture choices; and identify technical risks early.</li>
<li><strong>Solution Launch &amp; Landing:</strong> Own the "Day 0" launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value. Own production readiness across data quality, testing, security, performance, and operations. Work with the team to diagnose issues and drive them to resolution.</li>
<li><strong>Strategic Handoff &amp; Growth:</strong> Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement. Codify reusable solution patterns and bring field insights back to Product and Engineering.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>What we look for</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Executive Presence &amp; Communication:</strong> You are a trusted advisor with strong executive presence and excellent communication skills. You are confident and humble, can build rapport quickly, and can help senior stakeholders make difficult decisions.</li>
<li><strong>Product Judgment &amp; Delivery:</strong> You can define what to build and why, write strong product requirements, prioritize engineering work, manage scope, and lead complex agile software projects from an ambiguous problem to a measurable outcome.</li>
<li><strong>Technical Fluency &amp; Architecture Judgment:</strong> You understand modern data and AI architectures, including cloud platforms, data pipelines, data models, distributed systems, APIs, security and governance, machine learning, and generative AI application patterns. You can lead architecture discussions, evaluate trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions.</li>
<li><strong>Hands-on Technical Ability:</strong> You are proficient in at least one language such as Python, Java, or SQL. You can explore data, work in notebooks, read and review code and pipelines, build or adapt prototypes, and contribute meaningfully to troubleshooting.</li>
<li><strong>Relevant Experience:</strong> Typically 7+ years of experience delivering complex, customer-facing data, analytics, AI, or software engagements, or equivalent experience as a founder or technical builder. You have helped deliver data, machine learning, or generative AI systems into production and understand the integration, operational, and adoption challenges that appear in real environments. Experience in a high-growth technology company, forward-deployed organization, or leading consultancy is valuable. You enjoy working onsite with customers (often 25-50%, sometimes higher) to drive delivery.</li>
</ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>About Databricks</strong></p>
<p><span>Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&amp;T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/databricks">LinkedIn</a>, <a href="https://x.com/databricks">X</a>, <a href="https://www.youtube.com/@Databricks">YouTube</a>, and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/databricksinc/?hl=en">Instagram</a>.<br><br><strong>Benefits<br><br></strong></span>At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. For specific details on the benefits offered in your region click <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/154un3e8Xav4BceOSlcYFZRGEuQI54xMxVydRwQn54eQ/edit?usp=sharing">here</a>.<br><br></p>
<p><strong>Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion</strong></p>
<p>At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards. Individuals looking for employment at Databricks are considered without regard to age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, veteran status, and other protected characteristics.</p>
<p><strong>Compliance</strong></p>
<p><strong><span>If access to export-controlled technology or source code is required for performance of job duties, it is within Employer's discretion whether to apply for a U.S. government license for such positions, and Employer may decline to proceed with an applicant on this basis alone.</span></strong></p></div>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/databricks-deployment-strategist">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/databricks-deployment-strategist</a></p>

","id":"cf13d272-92ac-407d-89bf-7f20d20f7961","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with organizations of 1,000+ employees. This is a “Hunter” role with significant inbound and SDR support.

• Research and prospect into target accounts, building strategic account plans that map stakeholders, priorities, and opportunities for long-term growth.

• Lead complex enterprise sales cycles, proactively engaging multiple stakeholders, including CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Product leaders, platform teams, developer experience leaders, procurement, security, and legal.

• Build multi-threaded relationships across each account and develop multiple internal champions to secure new deals and support expansion over time.

• Achieve and exceed revenue targets while maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data for long-cycle deals.

• Structure and negotiate agreements that support customer adoption, expansion, and long-term success.

• Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges at scale, including how AI is reshaping software development in large organizations.

• Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

• Build business cases and return-on-investment (ROI) narratives that resonate with executive buyers.

• Partner closely with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations, proofs of concept, and integration planning.

• Collaborate with Customer Success to support retention and identify expansion opportunities across business units, while sharing customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

• Travel up to 30% of the time to meet existing and prospective customers in your regional market, strengthen relationships, and support business growth.

Royalty Operations owns the operations behind Spotify’s royalty process across music, audiobooks, lyrics, and creator content. We implement content licenses in Spotify’s proprietary royalty systems, calculate and report royalties to our rightsholder partners, provide analytics to Accounting stakeholders, and serve as the go-to team for royalty questions across the company. As our business grows more complex, we’re focused on staying accurate and on time while getting faster and more flexible through scripting, Gen AI, and agentic workflows.
","id":"a4651332-6400-40e8-8c22-5491e7a34161","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Build a deep understanding of Spotify’s label, publishing, lyrics, and audiobook contracts, how they’re implemented in our royalty systems, and how they flow into royalty calculations, downstream datasets, and reporting.
  • Use the team’s internal AI tooling to configure contracts in Spotify’s royalty systems and test financial outputs for accuracy before sign-off from Commercial Accounting.
  • Lead data analyses to answer royalty questions from internal teams such as Legal & Licensing and Finance, and from external partners such as rightsholders and back offices.
  • Support month-end royalty close by reviewing checks, validating calculation outputs, and escalating risks or issues.
  • Run month-end analytics, from generating the data and deck to providing commentary on fluxes, to support Content Accounting’s sign-off on final royalty figures.
  • Help build new capabilities for the team, contributing directly to how our internal AI tooling evolves as Spotify’s business grows.
  • Partner closely with Legal & Licensing, Commercial Accounting, Content Accounting, and Financial Engineering.
"},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have a background in Finance, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • You have 1+ years of experience in a data analyst or technical operations role. Experience in a royalty-related role at a record label, digital service provider, or music publisher is a plus.

    ","categories":{"commitment":"Permanent","department":"Engineering","location":"Stockholm","team":"Platform","allLocations":["Stockholm","London"]},"createdAt":1790590791162,"descriptionPlain":"Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next. These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide. This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.   ","description":"

    Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next.

    These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide.

    This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.

Hold them to a high bar for correctness, performance and reliability.
  • Build Data Pipelines: Develop and run the batch and streaming pipelines that keep our metadata current, processing platform events and audit logs to capture how data is created and changed, and turning lineage and metadata into data products other teams build on.
  • Own Projects End to End: Turn what the teams using our platform need into technical designs, drive them through delivery and rollout, and own the results once they're in production.
  • Keep the Platform Healthy: Take part in on-call for critical services, build in observability and quality checks by default, and use automation, including AI tooling, to reduce toil for the team and our users.

We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job.

We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next.

    We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data.   • Own quarterly and annual revenue targets for your client portfolio, managing your sales pipeline and identifying opportunities for sustainable growth.
  • Build and strengthen relationships with media agencies and advertising clients, understanding their business priorities and positioning Spotify as a valuable strategic partner.

    Spotify is looking for a culturally fluent, strategically sharp, and creative Communications Lead to shape and share our story across MENAT+. You’ll lead communications across the Middle East, North Africa, Türkiye, and Pakistan, helping Spotify strengthen its reputation, champion regional creators, and show up in ways that feel relevant to the audiences and communities we serve.

    Reporting to the Head of Communications, SAMEA, you’ll work closely with regional leadership and Spotify’s global communications teams across consumer, corporate, policy, industry, executive, and internal communications. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who combines strategic judgment with hands-on execution and knows how to navigate culturally dynamic, fast-moving markets.

    ","id":"c152d042-642d-4a48-862b-8be8d6cdc819","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Shape and execute an integrated communications strategy for MENAT+, putting regional creators, audiences, and culture at the heart of Spotify’s storytelling.
  • Be a trusted communications partner to regional leadership, providing clear counsel on business priorities, reputation, emerging issues, and high-impact moments.
  • Anticipate reputational opportunities and risks and help Spotify respond thoughtfully and effectively as cultural, media, policy, and regulatory dynamics evolve.
  • Lead creator-first and earned-first storytelling that builds fandom, discovery, and cultural relevance, finding compelling stories in emerging scenes, communities, and moments that matter locally.
  • Partner with Music, Podcasts, Product, Growth, Marketing, Public Affairs, and other teams to develop communications that support Spotify’s regional priorities.
  • Connect MENAT+ priorities and perspectives with Spotify’s global communications strategy, while translating global priorities in ways that resonate with local audiences.
  • Lead corporate, executive, internal, and B2B communications, including executive positioning, thought leadership, media engagement, and strategic messaging.
  • Lead agency relationships and budgets with creativity and discipline, developing efficient approaches that deliver high-quality, locally relevant work across a diverse geographic footprint.

  • You’re curious about music, creators, culture, technology, and the changing media landscape, and you bring a collaborative, resourceful, and hands-on approach to getting great work done.

    Music Expression builds the tools artists use to show who they are on Spotify and to connect with fans. A song doesn't have to be just a track in a list. On Spotify it can come with a looping Canvas visual, a music video, a vertical-video clip from the artist, or a countdown to a new release. Release day can become a shared Listening Party. Every one of those things was built by this org. Each squad owns part of the artist-to-fan journey.

    The work runs from video pipelines and serving infrastructure through mobile and web clients to rights systems, so engineers get real depth and range. Product, design, data science, research and product marketing work inside the squads, and they work directly with artists and labels.     If this role excites you but you don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds.

","description":"

    Spotify is building the next generation of advertising, connecting brands with audiences through audio, video, and experiences that are deeply embedded in people's lives. As our advertising business evolves, demonstrating the impact of advertising on Spotify, and helping advertisers achieve better outcomes, will be critical to our long-term success.

    We are seeking a Head of Measurement & Advertising Effectiveness to define how Spotify proves the value of its advertising, advances measurement science, and makes advertiser effectiveness a lasting competitive advantage.

    Reporting directly to the SVP of Advertising, you will be a member of the global Advertising leadership team, operating within a business with end-to-end P&L accountability. You will play an influential role in shaping our strategy, guiding investment priorities, and strengthening the value we deliver to advertisers.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a differentiated measurement and effectiveness organization at a time when the industry is being reshaped by AI, evolving privacy expectations, and increasing demand for measurable business outcomes. We are looking for a leader who combines scientific rigor, strategic vision, commercial judgment, and exceptional people leadership—and who can represent Spotify as a credible and influential voice in the industry.

    ","id":"01b41b49-7d43-4933-9ba7-06ebe0a2a749","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Build and transform the function. Set Spotify’s global measurement and effectiveness vision across brand, performance, and full-funnel advertising, and fundamentally build and elevate our capabilities to get there.
  • Advance measurement science. Lead our approach to incrementality, causal inference, experimentation, attribution, marketing mix modeling, and brand lift, and set rigorous standards for how we measure advertiser outcomes.
  • Define what we need to prove. Set the scientific requirements for measuring advertising impact on Spotify, and influence investment priorities with Product, Engineering, and Data Science, who own building the solutions.
  • Turn evidence into advertiser growth. Build marketing science and consulting capabilities that help advertisers understand and improve their results on Spotify, and partner with commercial leaders to turn that evidence into deeper relationships and smarter investment decisions.
  • Tailor measurement by industry. Develop approaches that reflect the distinct goals and challenges of advertisers in key verticals.
  • Build research and partnerships. Set an ambitious research agenda, develop relationships with leading measurement and technology partners, and advance independent validation and new approaches.
  • Lead what’s next. Anticipate how AI, new methods, and ecosystem shifts will change measurement, and position Spotify to lead rather than follow.
  • Shape industry thinking. Go beyond representing Spotify to help shape how the industry approaches effectiveness and measurement standards, through direct engagement with CMOs and agency leaders, seats on industry boards, major conference stages, and thought leadership.
  • Build an exceptional organization. Design, scale, and lead a high-performing global team spanning measurement strategy, marketing science, advertiser consulting, research, and partnerships.
  • Shape Advertising leadership decisions. Bring scientific expertise, advertiser insight, and an evidence-based perspective to the leadership team’s strategic choices and long-term priorities.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You’re an accomplished senior leader in advertising measurement, marketing science, or advertiser effectiveness, ideally at a leading ad platform, technology company, or measurement organization.
  • You have a track record of setting strategy, building or transforming capabilities, and delivering impact at scale.
  • You have deep expertise in incrementality, causal inference, experimentation, attribution, and marketing effectiveness, and the judgment to weigh each method’s strengths, limits, and practical uses.
  • You understand how advertisers make investment decisions and how measurement drives media allocation, confidence, and growth.
  • You pair scientific rigor with commercial thinking, turning complex evidence into clear priorities, compelling narratives, and actionable recommendations.
  • You understand the product, data, technology, and privacy factors shaping modern measurement, and you’ve successfully influenced cross-functional investments.
  • You’re excited by the measurement challenges of audio, video, and podcasts: formats where traditional click-based attribution falls short.

    Spotify’s mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.

    Data is a means to an end, and Spotify extracts value from data through application. The Data Platform Studio helps Spotify win by enabling the application of data in an intuitive and efficient way.

    Data Platform is responsible for how data is collected, processed, stored, governed, and made available to the thousands of engineers, data scientists, analysts, and machine learning practitioners who build Spotify’s products. As AI agents increasingly generate code, write data pipelines, and power personalized user experiences, Data Platform sits at the center of one of the most important infrastructure domains at Spotify.

    We're looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the team responsible for Spotify’s data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage capabilities. In this role, you'll own the strategy and roadmap for a critical part of Spotify's data ecosystem, helping users discover, understand, trust, and safely use data at scale. You'll work closely with engineers, designers, data scientists, and product teams across Spotify to make working with data faster, safer, and more intuitive.

  • Evaluate and deliver solutions through building, buying, or integrating third-party products and capabilities.

  • Help shape how Spotify approaches metadata, governance, discoverability, lineage, and trust in an increasingly AI-driven world.
  • Stay informed on industry trends across data platforms, developer tools, AI/ML infrastructure, analytics, and data governance.

    Spotify’s mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.

    Data is a means to an end, and Spotify extracts value from data through application. The Data Platform Studio helps Spotify win by enabling the application of data in an intuitive and efficient way.

    Data Platform is responsible for how data is collected, processed, stored, governed, and made available to the thousands of engineers, data scientists, analysts, and machine learning practitioners who build Spotify’s products. As AI agents increasingly generate code, write data pipelines, and power personalized user experiences, Data Platform sits at the center of one of the most important infrastructure domains at Spotify.

    We're looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the team responsible for Spotify’s data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage capabilities. In this role, you'll own the strategy and roadmap for a critical part of Spotify's data ecosystem, helping users discover, understand, trust, and safely use data at scale. You'll work closely with engineers, designers, data scientists, and product teams across Spotify to make working with data faster, safer, and more intuitive.

    • Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on the use of generative music tools within the artistic community.     • Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for the use of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

    • Lead Spotify India's consumer retention and engagement marketing strategy across the listener lifecycle, from new and active users to dormant and lapsed listeners.

    • Identify the key drivers of disengagement and churn, and develop targeted strategies that encourage repeat listening and long-term retention.

    • Build tailored retention and re-engagement strategies for different listener segments, using behavioural insights, preferences and engagement patterns.

    • Create personalised listener journeys that connect audiences with relevant music, artists, content and Spotify features.

    • Partner with Data Science, Analytics and Consumer Insights teams to uncover engagement opportunities and turn consumer insights into actionable marketing initiatives.

    • Define and track key performance indicators, including retention, churn, reactivation, daily and monthly active users, and engagement. Use experimentation to measure incremental impact and continuously improve results.

    • Collaborate with Product, Music, Brand, Media and Consumer Marketing teams to develop a connected retention roadmap that brings together product experiences, music releases, artists and cultural moments.

    • Translate insights and performance trends into clear recommendations that influence marketing priorities and drive measurable business outcomes.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are comfortable balancing long-term strategy with hands-on execution, adapting your approach as you learn what works.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe.     Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.

     

    You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.

     

    We are a distributed team that values curiosity, sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous learning. We teach and learn from one another, adapt as the threat landscape changes, and focus our effort according to business needs and risk.

    ","id":"cb29d857-395b-401d-9749-367e666ff870","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Identify detection opportunities, define clear telemetry requirements, and partner with the detection infrastructure squad and data owners to make the signals needed for detection and investigation available.

    • Develop, test, tune, and maintain detections across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, email, and other security-relevant environments.

    • Investigate and prioritize alerts, determine their security impact, and participate in incident containment and remediation.

    • Build repeatable investigation workflows and playbooks for alert triage, evidence collection, decision-making, escalation, containment, and response.

    • Improve proactive threat-identification and threat-hunting capabilities using internal telemetry and external threat intelligence.

    • Create cutting-edge AI workflows for Detection and Response that enrich alerts, gather and analyze evidence, guide investigations, and automate repetitive response work while preserving appropriate human judgment and oversight.

    • Measure detection effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and tune detections to balance security value, fidelity, and analyst workload.

    • Use SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and related security platforms to research threats, develop detections, investigate alerts, and validate security outcomes.

    • Share knowledge, document decisions, and communicate security findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in an ambiguous and rapidly changing environment.

    • You have 3+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, detection engineering, or closely related work.

    • You understand how analysts triage and investigate alerts and how detection quality affects their decisions and workload.

    • You know how to create and tune detections based on attacker behavior, available telemetry, and an expected investigation path.

    • You are experienced with security platforms such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or comparable monitoring and response technologies.

    • You can write code or use an automation platform to analyze security telemetry, enrich alerts, build investigation workflows, and remove repetitive work. Experience with Python or a similar language is valuable.

    • You understand modern detection-as-code practices, including GitHub, peer review, CI/CD, testing, and safely managing production detection content.

    • You have experience working with at least one major cloud platform, such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure.

    • You understand common threats affecting SaaS-oriented corporate and production environments.

    • You care about clear documentation, inclusive collaboration, and explaining security concepts to people with different backgrounds and levels of expertise.

    • You are excited to create and critically evaluate cutting-edge AI workflows for detection development, alert triage, security investigations, and response, while applying sound security judgment and appropriate human oversight.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

    "}],"text":"Security Engineer - Detection and Response","country":"US","workplaceType":"remote","opening":"","openingPlain":"","descriptionBody":"

    Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.

     

    You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Security engineers at Spotify help protect our environment and more than 700 million users. Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

    As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

     

    ","id":"1ee5dcb7-a5fe-465b-91da-d42ebab374c8","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Build and improve agentic AI workflows that turn security vulnerability findings into tested, review-ready code changes for engineering teams across Spotify.

    • Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the quality of automated fixes, including correctness, completeness, safety, build and test success, and pull request merge rates.

    • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.

    • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

    • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

    • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

    • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have experience in software engineering, particularly within security engineering, developer experience, or internal infrastructure.

    • You can confidently read, understand, and write code in one or more languages such as Java, Python, Scala, C++, or TypeScript.

    • You have experience designing and building scalable systems, with an understanding of software architecture and reliable engineering practices.

    • You have worked with agentic AI systems or AI-assisted development workflows and understand how to apply them to real-world engineering challenges.

    • You understand common security risks, attack vectors, and vulnerabilities, including those affecting AI and machine learning systems, and approaches to mitigating them.

    • You have experience integrating security tools or automated workflows into production engineering environments.

    • You are familiar with agentic AI frameworks and approaches to evaluating the quality, reliability, and safety of AI-generated outputs.

    • You enjoy collaborating across teams, learning from feedback, and navigating ambiguity. You're comfortable experimenting with new approaches while balancing innovation with thoughtful security decisions.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    • This role is based in Toronto

    • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

    We are looking for a Senior Accountant to join our Global Record to Report (RTR) team. Our close is evolving fast, and we’re looking for someone who combines strong accounting judgment with curiosity about how AI and automation can change how we work, and who wants to help build that future rather than wait for it.

    As a Senior Accountant on the General Ledger team, you will own key close processes end to end, from preparation and analysis to explaining results to partners across Finance. You will use data and AI tools to remove manual work, spend more of your time on review and insight, and help shape how a lean, global team scales.

    ","id":"3616d255-dd0f-4771-a0c8-92bdc2abdccd","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

     

    • Own the monthly and quarterly close for your areas, delivering accurate IFRS results and clear, insight-driven flux commentary
    • Use AI tools and data (BigQuery, SQL, LLM-based assistants) to automate preparation, speed up analysis, and redirect time toward review and judgment
    • Design, build, and maintain lightweight automations and AI-assisted workflows, and partner with Financial Engineering on larger system changes
    • Make sure automated and AI-assisted processes stay accurate, explainable, and well-controlled, including SOX controls and audit evidence
    • Act as a go-to partner for FP&A, Tax, Treasury, Procurement, AP, and business teams, turning ad hoc requests into scalable, self-serve solutions
    • Support external and internal audits for your areas and keep RTR processes and documentation current
    • Share knowledge and coach teammates on both accounting and new ways of working
    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
    • You have 4+ years of month-end close or general ledger experience at a global, publicly traded company, with solid IFRS knowledge
    • You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; a CPA or equivalent is a plus
    • You bring strong accounting judgment and can research and resolve accounting questions independently
    • You’re comfortable working directly with data; experience with SQL and BigQuery is strongly preferred, or you have a clear willingness to learn quickly
    • You have hands-on experience using AI tools to improve your work, or strong curiosity to start, plus the judgment to know when not to trust the output
    • You have an automation mindset: you notice repetitive work and want to remove it
    • You understand upstream and downstream processes (AP, Procurement, Treasury) and how they affect the general ledger
    • You have experience with ERP systems (NetSuite preferred; Oracle or SAP also relevant)
    • You’re a clear communicator who can explain accounting and data topics to non-specialists and keep priorities on track during close

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.

    Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.

    Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    ","id":"babebec3-0061-4c39-a4ad-c51a54d23567","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
  • Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
  • Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
  • Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
  • Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
  • Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
  • You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
  • You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
  • You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
  • You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
  • You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
  • You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
  • You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.

    We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.

    You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale. You’ll partner with subject-matter experts, people leaders, and Learning & Inclusion colleagues on company-wide initiatives, from leadership development to programs that bring Spotify’s values to life.

    ","id":"9d1c90b5-a8a4-4218-b2f3-7bbaefae7fd1","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation.
  • Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions.
  • Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles.
  • Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences.
  • Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify.
  • Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms.
  • Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging.
  • Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data.
  • Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change.
  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

  • You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content.
  • You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate.
  • You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent.
  • You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences.
  • You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes.
  • You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners.
  • You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience.
  • You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI.
  • You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

    Spotify is shaping the future of advertising by connecting brands with fans through audio, video, and experiences that are part of people's everyday lives. As our advertising business grows, we're focused on bringing innovative products to market, helping advertisers succeed, and turning new ideas into meaningful business growth.

    We're looking for a Senior Director, Global Advertising Product Marketing to lead the next chapter of our global Advertising Product Marketing team. Reporting to the Head of Advertising Business Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to shape product strategy, strengthen our market position, and help advertisers get more value from Spotify.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a product marketing function with a clear voice in product decisions and a direct impact on business growth. You'll bring customer insights into product development, establish a disciplined approach to go-to-market execution and product adoption, create compelling reasons for advertisers to choose Spotify, and help a global team deliver measurable results.

    ","id":"b9533f31-7bff-43f6-aaf0-60003f017d88","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for global Advertising Product Marketing, connecting advertiser needs, product innovation, competitive insights, and business growth.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to bring customer and market insights into product decisions and turn innovation into solutions advertisers value.
  • Lead global go-to-market strategies for Spotify's advertising products, including brand and performance advertising, self-service, programmatic, and emerging solutions. Own product positioning, messaging, packaging, launches, and adoption.
  • Build a deeper understanding of advertisers, agencies, buying behaviors, and the competitive landscape. Use these insights to identify opportunities, influence product priorities, and strengthen Spotify's position in the market.
  • Drive product adoption and commercial growth by identifying customer needs, addressing barriers to adoption, and partnering with teams to improve product usage, retention, and revenue. Define clear measures of success and use results to guide future decisions.
  • Turn complex advertising technology, data, and measurement capabilities into clear, differentiated customer value propositions tied to measurable business outcomes. Partner with Business Marketing to create a consistent story across products and help advertisers understand the impact Spotify can deliver.
  • Strengthen how products move from development to market. Establish clear processes, shared accountability, and measures of readiness that help teams make informed decisions about when to launch, scale, improve, or stop initiatives.
  • Equip Sales and regional teams with the insights, messaging, and tools they need to bring Spotify's advertising solutions to customers. 
  • Work with Measurement and Advertising Effectiveness teams to connect product capabilities with credible evidence of advertiser outcomes, and feed that evidence back into product decisions
  • Explore how AI, automation, and emerging advertising technologies can improve our products, customer experiences, and product marketing practices and identify opportunities to rethink how Spotify develops, positions, and scales its advertising solutions.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing global Product Marketing organization, attracting outstanding talent, strengthening strategic and commercial capabilities, and creating a culture of creativity, accountability, collaboration, and measurable impact.

    ","id":"ee45924c-894c-4ea0-9c93-c5221894063f","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Define the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for session management across Spotify’s clients, device types, and strategic partner integrations.
  • Use research, data, and feedback from users and developers to identify access friction and prioritize improvements with the greatest potential impact.
  • Improve how sessions are established, maintained, and ended, balancing reliable access with account protection, privacy, and user control.
  • Shape device connection, session transfer, and partner authorization experiences, including clear consent when an app requests access or additional capabilities.
  • Partner with engineering to make session and access capabilities reusable and easier to adopt through APIs, client components, documentation, and clear integration guidance.
  • Work across client, device, and partner teams to understand different needs, align priorities, and carry improvements through delivery and adoption.
  • Define success measures for access quality, user friction, developer experience, and adoption, connecting those measures to meaningful user and business outcomes.
  • Make thoughtful trade-offs between immediate experience improvements, long-term technical investment, security, and privacy while providing teams with clear direction and context.

  • Own the quality bar for Spotify’s AI voice models, defining what “good enough” means for different products, audiences, languages and use cases.
  • Independently design evaluation rubrics and build an evaluation approach that measures qualities such as naturalness, tone, pacing, pronunciation, accent, audio quality and overall experience.
  • Plan and carry out evaluation campaigns, turning qualitative and quantitative findings into clear recommendations for Voice Production, Speak and product teams.
  • Establish an ongoing evaluation rhythm, including when and how we reassess model quality as our technology and products evolve.
  • Benchmark Spotify’s AI voices against third-party models and competitors to understand where our experiences lead, where they differ and where there are opportunities to improve.
  • Help determine appropriate quality trade-offs as Spotify expands into additional languages and regions, considering the product use case and needs of each market.
  • Partner closely with voice experts, machine learning teams, product partners and vendors to maintain a consistent quality bar across demanding and sometimes competing priorities.
  • Surface the most meaningful gaps in model performance and use evaluation insights to help influence future research and technical priorities.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. Our team builds and operates the authorization and permissioning systems that enable creators and their teams to securely access and manage their presence across Spotify. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

    This is a backend-focused role working on systems that sit on a critical path for Spotify's creator ecosystem. You'll help us evolve these systems as they grow in scale and complexity, bringing strong backend engineering expertise while collaborating across product, frontend, and data when needed.

    ","id":"e04833c0-9cff-4b5e-b217-91a3bcb57051","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do:","content":"

    • Design, build, deploy, and operate scalable backend services that power authorization, permissions, and team management across Spotify.

    • Take ownership of critical systems that enable creators, teams, agents, licensors, and other partners to securely access and manage the right content and capabilities.

    • Evolve our backend architecture to support continued growth in users, use cases, and Spotify products while maintaining high standards for reliability, performance, and security.

    • Improve the systems and workflows that enable creators to gain access to their content, profiles, and teams.

    • Make thoughtful technical decisions and trade-offs, balancing long-term architecture with solutions that meet current product and business needs.

    • Partner with engineers and cross-functional collaborators across Spotify to understand authorization needs and build reusable platform capabilities.

    • Contribute to frontend experiences and data-related work when useful, while bringing deep expertise and leadership to backend engineering.

    • Raise engineering quality through strong technical judgment, design discussions, operational excellence, and knowledge sharing across the team.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are:","content":"

    • You have deep experience designing, building, and operating backend services, with strong knowledge of Java or comparable backend technologies.

    We are looking for a strategic public policy professional to join Spotify’s Global Government Affairs team in New York City. The Government Affairs team helps Spotify understand the global and local policy landscape, advocates on issues important to our business and users, and works to anticipate and mitigate policy and regulatory risks.

    In this role, you’ll work closely with Government Affairs colleagues and teams across Spotify to develop positions on public policy proposals and strategies to advance them. You’ll report to the Director of Government Affairs, US & Canada, with a particular focus on state and local policy.

    ","id":"1961fa91-bdba-450a-bfb6-fc8d8d5c9e9c","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Design and execute policymaker engagement strategies that strengthen Spotify’s relationships across priority jurisdictions, with a focus on New York City, New York State, and other key states.
  • Develop expertise on public policy issues with commercial and reputational importance to Spotify, including tax, artificial intelligence, content moderation, and emerging policy matters.
  • Identify and assess priority state and local public policy issues affecting Spotify, and partner with your manager and US Government Affairs colleagues to develop effective advocacy strategies.
  • Collaborate with teams across Spotify, including Legal, Communications, Social Impact, Product, Compliance, and Trust & Safety, to understand business priorities, develop clear policy narratives, and shape approaches to key policy issues.
  • Build relationships and partnerships with external organizations, including trade associations and civil society organizations, to advance engagement and thought leadership on priority public policy issues.
  • Represent Spotify with policymakers, government officials, industry peers, and other external stakeholders in support of the company’s policy priorities.

    • You have experience developing public policy strategies related to the technology sector and can translate complex policy developments into clear business implications.
    • You have experience engaging senior government officials, private-sector leaders, and public policy professionals.
    • You can develop and execute effective advocacy strategies while balancing multiple stakeholders and priorities.
    • You communicate clearly in writing and conversation and can adapt your approach for policymakers, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
    • You build collaborative relationships across functions and levels, approach problems with sound judgment and integrity, and are comfortable operating in a changing policy environment.
    • You are able to travel throughout the United States as needed, including occasionally on short notice.
